$comment: Golden conversation for the HelloCamera phone-client conformance kit. Meta-format: docs/conformance/README.md. This conversation asserts a phone-local projection that the closed socket cannot carry; it is exercised by the phoneLocalProjection block, not by later wire messages.
title: Phone-local disconnect projection requires no server revision
summary: Socket loss cannot be represented by a desktop snapshot. A phone that has accepted v2 MUST derive a local presentation immediately on close: phase recovering; retain the accepted intention and Instruction but render its freshness as may_be_outdated; show recovering Activity; clear overlays, every protocol-owned action, and the complete visual-guidance lane/artifact; and keep camera controls, intention editing, and the local shutter usable. This local projection does not allocate or alter sessionId or stateRevision and is never sent to the desktop.

steps.note: Accepted sessionId and v2 wire mode. (PROTOCOL_V2.md §4.2)

message.acceptedIntention: A confident full-body portrait at sunset

instruction.text: Photographer: move one step to your left.

steps.note: Last valid server projection: a current Instruction, an overlay set, and an offered action. This is the projection retained (as may_be_outdated) after disconnect.
The WebSocket is lost. No server message can arrive. The phone MUST derive the local projection below immediately on the close callback, using phone monotonic time only. (PROTOCOL_V2.md §4.3)

phoneLocalProjection.retainedIntention: A confident full-body portrait at sunset

retainedInstruction.text: Photographer: move one step to your left.

outcome: The phone keeps camera controls, intention editing, and the local shutter usable. It does not allocate or alter sessionId or stateRevision. On a new connection, a valid v1 result received before v2 acceptance replaces the local projection under v1 rules; after acceptance, the first valid complete coaching_state_v2 atomically replaces it. Invalid or stale input leaves the local disconnected projection intact.
